correctness.rationale: The proof partitions all integers with \(\Omega\le2\) into primes, prime squares, and products of two distinct primes. Prime endpoints are excluded by divisor-sum size. After isolating the even member as \(2p\), the four remaining square/product orientations reduce to two impossible quadratics, \((q-2)(r-2)=-3\), or \((q-2)(r-2)=3\); the last has only \(q=3,r=5\), yielding \((14,15)\).

value.rationale: The Erdős--Sierpiński equation is a classical open problem, and total prime-factor count is a standard intrinsic complexity measure. The theorem completely closes its first composite multiplicative layer and gives an algebraic explanation for the uniqueness of the first known pair 14,15 in that layer, rather than merely extending a computational cutoff.
